title: Daily Practice: Ch 8 Heredity
subject: Science
instructions: One day at a time, about 25 minutes each: Day 1 on the day you study the chapter, then Day 2 and Day 3. Write answers in your notebook and check them with the key the same day. Copy every mistake into your error log.
In every cross, write the parents, then the gametes, then a checkerboard, then the ratio. Never skip the gametes step!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the pairs of contrasting traits Mendel studied in garden peas?
questions.answer: (d) red and black seeds. (Seed colour in his work was yellow or green.)

questions.q: When two pure-breeding plants with contrasting traits are crossed, the trait seen in all the F_{1} plants is called:
questions.answer: (b) dominant

questions.q: The genotype of a pure-breeding short pea plant is:
questions.answer: (c) tt: a recessive trait shows only when both copies are recessive

questions.q: In a cross between Tt and tt pea plants, the percentage of short plants expected is:
questions.answer: (c) 50%: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in a 1 : 1 ratio

questions.q: What is heredity? What is a gene?
questions.answer: Heredity is the passing of traits (characters) from parents to their offspring. A gene is a section of DNA that carries the information for making one protein, and so controls a trait.

questions.q: Every person has two copies of each gene. Where does each copy come from?
questions.answer: One copy comes from the father and one from the mother, through their germ cells (sperm and egg).

questions.q: A pea plant with yellow seeds (Yy) is self-pollinated. Show the cross with a checkerboard, and give the genotypic and phenotypic ratios of the offspring.
questions.answer:
Parents: Yy × Yy. Gametes: Y, y from each parent.
Checkerboard: YY, Yy, Yy, yy.
Genotypic ratio: 1 YY : 2 Yy : 1 yy.
Phenotypic ratio: 3 yellow : 1 green.

questions.q: Explain, with an example of each: (a) a pure-breeding plant, (b) a hybrid, (c) the F_{2} generation.
questions.answer:
(a) A plant that gives offspring with the same trait generation after generation when self-pollinated, e.g. a TT tall plant.
(b) The offspring of two pure-breeding parents with contrasting traits, e.g. Tt from TT × tt.
(c) The generation obtained by self-pollinating the F_{1} plants, e.g. Tt × Tt gives F_{2} in the ratio 3 tall : 1 short.

questions.q: Which cross will give offspring that ALL show the dominant trait?
questions.answer: (c) TT × tt: every offspring is Tt

questions.q: The 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio in the F_{2} of Mendel's dihybrid cross shows that:
options: the two traits are always inherited together
only dominant traits are passed on
the two traits are inherited independently
questions.answer: (d) the two traits are inherited independently

questions.q: Plant height depends on a growth hormone. The gene for height controls:
options: how well the enzyme that makes the hormone works
the number of chromosomes in the plant
questions.answer: (a) If the gene makes an efficient enzyme, more hormone is made and the plant grows tall.

questions.q: A cross between two tall pea plants gives offspring in the ratio 3 tall : 1 short. What are the genotypes of the parents?
questions.answer: Both are Tt. Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: 3 tall to 1 short.

questions.q: A cross between two pea plants gives 50% round seeds and 50% wrinkled seeds. What are the genotypes of the parents?
questions.answer: Rr × rr. The gametes are R and r from one parent, and only r from the other, so the offspring are Rr and rr in a 1 : 1 ratio.

questions.q:
Mendel's F_{1} plants from the dihybrid cross had the genotype RrYy.
(a) Write the four kinds of gametes they make.
(b) What fraction of the F_{2} seeds are round and green?
(c) What fraction are wrinkled and yellow?
questions.answer:
(a) RY, Ry, rY and ry
(b) 3/16
(c) 3/16
(The full F_{2} ratio is 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green.)

questions.q: A tall pea plant could be TT or Tt. How can you find out which it is? Explain with crosses.
questions.answer:
Cross it with a short plant (tt).
If it is TT: TT × tt gives all Tt, so all the offspring are tall.
If it is Tt: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt, so about half the offspring are short.

sections.title: Day 3: Sex determination, mixed practice and challenge

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** The sex of a child is decided at the time of fertilisation.
**Reason (R):** Whether the fertilising sperm carries an X or a Y chromosome decides the sex of the child.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (a) Both are true, and R explains A.

questions.q: In some reptiles, the sex of the young is decided by:
options: the temperature at which the eggs are kept
questions.answer: (a) the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are incubated

questions.q: Which genotype belongs to a pure-breeding plant with round, yellow seeds?
questions.answer: (b) RRYY: pure-breeding means both copies of each gene are the same

questions.q: A couple has three daughters and is expecting a fourth child. Some relatives blame the mother for not having a son.

subparts.q: Which sex chromosome does the mother pass on to every child?
subparts.answer: An X chromosome: all her eggs carry X.

subparts.q: Is the mother responsible for the sex of the children? Explain.
subparts.answer: No. The father's sperm carries either X or Y. A sperm with X gives a girl (XX) and one with Y gives a boy (XY), so the sex is decided by the sperm, not the egg.

subparts.q: What is the chance that the fourth child will be a boy?
subparts.answer: 50%, or 1 in 2. Each pregnancy is independent, so the three daughters born earlier do not change the chance.

questions.q:
A plant with round, green seeds (RRyy) is crossed with a plant with wrinkled, yellow seeds (rrYY).
(a) Write the gametes of each parent and the genotype and phenotype of the F_{1}.
(b) The F_{1} plants are self-pollinated. What fraction of the F_{2} will have round, yellow seeds?
(c) Which two combinations of traits in the F_{2} were not seen in either of the original parents?
questions.answer:
(a) Gametes: Ry from the RRyy parent and rY from the rrYY parent. F_{1}: RrYy, round and yellow.
(b) 9/16
(c) Round yellow and wrinkled green. (This shows that the two traits are inherited independently.)

questions.q: A trait can 'skip a generation': a grandparent and a grandchild show it, but the parent in between does not. Explain how this can happen.
questions.answer: The trait is recessive. The parent got one recessive copy from the grandparent but also a dominant copy, so the trait stayed hidden. If the child then receives a recessive copy from both parents, it shows the trait again.

closing: If you can do a dihybrid checkerboard in under 5 minutes, you're board-ready on this one!
